learned_from: answers the user gave to occasional calibration questions and to GAIA's 'was that the right call?' check-ins

answers.q: If another app or person already alerted you about something (bank SMS, PagerDuty call, airline app, a colleague) and you saw or acknowledged it, should I also tell you?
answers.a: No, don't repeat it. Only tell me if you have something they didn't, or if I clearly haven't seen it.

answers.q: If you can see I've already done the thing a reminder or nudge is about, should it still go off?
answers.a: No. Just skip it. Reminders I set are for things I haven't done yet.

answers.q: When something newer replaces an older update (a newer email, a cancelled request, an approval I already gave elsewhere), what should happen to the old one?
answers.a: Drop the old one, only tell me the latest state.

answers.q: What is worth waking you up or interrupting a meeting for?
answers.a: Family health or safety, my home (leaks, alarms), money actually leaving or being blocked, travel on the day of travel, a person waiting on me right now, a hard deadline that closes before I'd normally see it, and anything I explicitly said to ping me the moment it happens.

answers.q: If a deadline closes before you'd normally check your messages, do you want to hear about it in time even if it's early or late?
answers.a: Yes, always in time. Missing a real deadline is worse than an extra message.

answers.q: During a call or meeting, what should come through?
answers.a: Only things about that meeting or the people in it, or real emergencies. Everything else after.

answers.q: When you ask me to watch something or ping you when it changes, do you want it straight away?
answers.a: Yes, that's why I asked. If I said 'the moment', even at night.
Fraud checks, failed or declined payments, anything that triggers a late fee or service cut-off, and large unexpected debits. Routine statements and small receipts can wait for the summary.
Only for things I'm actively watching, and only if I can still act. Otherwise batch them or skip.

answers.q: Mistakes you make on my behalf (wrong recipient, wrong booking)?
answers.a: Tell me as soon as you notice, while it can still be fixed.

answers.q: Anything private you should be careful with on my lock screen or in groups?
answers.a: Health, money, and anything about family or relationships. Keep previews generic.
Keep work out unless it's an emergency or something I'm waiting on. Personal and family things are fine.
